body.statement: For every rational \(p\) of coefficient height \(B\), \(\mathsf{Cert}\) terminates. If \(\mathfrak F(\mathcal S,L,H,p)=\varnothing\), it returns the exact refinement-enumeration ledger and, for every \(G\in\mathfrak G_{H,L}(\mathcal S)\) and every \(r\in\mathcal R_G\), a replayable real-algebraic elimination trace or rational Positivstellensatz identity proving \(\{\lambda\in\prod_a\Delta(\mathcal K_{G,r,a}):P_G(\lambda)=p\}=\varnothing\); these branch certificates jointly certify the empty fiber. If the fiber is nonempty, it returns for each endpoint a square-free integer isolating polynomial, a rational isolating interval, and an algebraic-weight endpoint-attaining SCM. In either branch its bit-operation count is \(R_{\Sigma}B^{O(1)}(s_{\max}D_{\max})^{O(k_{\max})}\). In the nonempty branch the endpoint algebraic degree is \(D_{\max}^{O(k_{\max})}\), and every output coefficient has bit length \(B(s_{\max}D_{\max})^{O(k_{\max})}\). The compiler derives \(R_{\Sigma},k_{\max},s_{\max},D_{\max}\) from \(d,H,L,E_{\mathcal S}^{\to},E_{\mathcal S}^{\leftrightarrow}\) and the raw branch catalogues. Thus, unlike the numerical \(\varepsilon\)-sharp output of Duarte et al., the algorithm either exactly rejects an incompatible observed law branch by branch or certifies exact attained endpoints and decodes checkable SCM witnesses.
body.justification: A total certifier must distinguish observational incompatibility from a nonempty identified set and provide exact evidence in either case.
body.gap: BasuPollackRoy1996 supplies generic real-quantifier-elimination complexity and GeigerMeek1999 applies elimination to small hidden-variable models; neither derives the causal encoding size, total empty-fiber certificate ledger, endpoint witness decoder, or refinement-union certificate, while DuarteEtAl2024 stops at numerical convergence.
body.consumer: Small summary-graph analyses obtain replayable incompatibility certificates or exact endpoint certificates that can be independently checked and used as gold standards for approximate solvers.
